newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian holding AvH taught Canadian lesson.
newsitem.headline: Belgian holding AvH taught Canadian lesson.

text.p: Belgian holding company Ackermans & van Haaren NV (AvH) said on Tuesday it had been taught a lesson in modesty by the downfall of its Canadian subsidiary Consumers Distributing.
The deconsolidation last year of AvH's 72.2 percent stake in the bankrupt Canadian retailer cost it 1.58 billion francs.

"We went further than we wanted, we took risks, but after two, three times, we decided to liquidate the company," AvH chief executive officer Luc Bertrand told a news conference on AvH's 1996 earnings.
"It's a lesson," chairman Erik van Baren said. "It makes us a bit more modest. It's good for the future not to think that everything we do succeeds," he said.
But AvH saved the day mainly through the sale of oil drilling contractor Forasol-Foramer NV to Houston-based oil well service and drilling contractor Pride Petroleum.
AvH, which had a 30 percent stake in Forasol, made a capital gain of 1.08 billion francs on the deal.
"It saved to a large extent our year," Bertrand said.
AvH said group net profit jumped 66 percent to 1.58 billion francs in 1996.
Bertrand said AvH was currently considering which strategic direction to take for its industrial activities.
But he added that AvH had no plans to sell any of its industrial units. He said the telecommunications sector could be a possible new area for investment.
"The competition is looking with envy to the companies in our group...but I can say that they are not for sale," Bertrand said.
He noted that AvH's entire strategy in recent years had been aimed at reducing its cyclical character.
He said AvH had now forged a group of strong stable shareholdings and entirely written down its financial debt.
The company is expecting a strong rise in 1997 current profit.
